text:
matt: starting canary for service=router-api version=v2.3.4 at 03:00-04:00 change window. deploying 5% -> 20% traffic split over 10m.

deploy-bot: :robot_face: Rollout requested (id: r-1234). Canary > 5% requires 2 manual approvals during changewindow. Current policy: guards=canary-guard_v2, fallback=stable. To approve: `/deploy approve r-1234 --by <name>`.

deploy-bot: config snippet:
```
{"traffic_split": [{"variant": "v2.3.4","pct": 5}, {"variant": "stable","pct": 95}], "step_duration": "10m"}
```

kim: quick question — why 5% start? last time 5% rounded down to 0 for some routes with low qps.

olivia: we use per-route weights, not global. if route qps < 100, 1% equals zero requests — we should ensure min-traffic buckets >0 (mds).

priya: also flag: dedicated customers hit quota calc differently, 5% could trigger quota throttle on their side. might need bypass tag.

sre-oncall: can we add a meltdown guard? last canary caused a CPU spike at t=2m. would prefer slow ramp: 2% -> 5% -> 10% -> 20%.

matt: good call. i'm fine with changing steps. can someone update canary config and we'll re-run approval.

jonah: i can update. question: deploy-bot only accepts single approve command per user, right?

deploy-bot: Correct. Each approver must run `/deploy approve r-1234` within the change window. Approvals are additive; 2 required. Approver trace saved to audit log.

kim: /deploy approve r-1234

matt: /deploy approve r-1234 — pushing ramp to 2% -> 5% -> 10% -> 20% over 40m. Watching telemetry: https://redwood.internal/telemetry/dashboards/router-api/canary/r-1234

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Rollout r-1234 approved by kim, matt. Starting canary.

deploy-bot: [update] step 1 (2%) started.

sre-oncall: monitoring cpu across clusters. will alert if >70% sustained for 3m.

deploy-bot: [metrics] after 2m: error_rate: 0.3% (+0.05), p95_latency: 120ms (+10ms). No regressions flagged.

olivia: looks stable. nice.

matt: nice work — keep an eye for anomalies. if anything pop, abort with `/deploy abort r-1234`.
